raw_response:
I have farmed these 12 mu for 35 years, and at 62 I know exactly what my husband and I can manage with just the two of us left at home. Cotton is our main livelihood and always has been, so I keep 7 mu in hybrid cotton—Guoxinmian gives good money, but it means thirteen rounds of spraying for bollworm and mites, plus hand-picking in autumn, and two old backs cannot handle more than that. The remaining 5 mu I run as wheat-maize double crop because the combine and no-till seeder let us manage it without breaking our bodies: the wheat is already in the ground from last autumn, rotary-tilled, and I will topdress nitrogen at green-up and irrigate four times to get my 1000 jin per mu; after harvest in early June we direct-seed hybrid maize with no tillage to save diesel and time, give it two irrigations, and spray twice. I do not over-fertilize—the soil here is decent after decades of care—so wheat gets about 20 kg nitrogen per mu, maize and cotton a bit less. We have the well, but pumping costs electricity, so I only water when the crops truly need it.
